'''Rondae Jaquan Hollis-Jefferson''' (born January 3, 1995) is an American-born naturalized Jordanian professional [[basketball]] player who last played for the [[Meralco Bolts]] of the [[East Asia Super League]] (EASL). After playing [[college basketball]] for the [[Arizona Wildcats men's basketball|Arizona Wildcats]], he was selected by the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA) in the [[2015 NBA draft]], and spent six seasons with the NBA before playing for four different basketball teams outside the United States. He has won three [[Philippine Basketball Association]] [[List of Philippine Basketball Association champions|championships]] as part of the [[TNT Tropang 5G|TNT Tropang Giga]], and three-time [[Bobby Parks PBA Best Import of the Conference award|Best Import of the Conference]] ([[2023 PBA Governors' Cup]], [[2024 PBA Governors' Cup]] and the [[2024–25 PBA Commissioner's Cup]]).

==Early life==
[[File:20130403 MCDAAG Rondae Hollis-Jefferson (2).JPG|thumb|left|upright|Hollis-Jefferson in the [[2013 McDonald's All-American Boys Game]]]]
Hollis-Jefferson was born and raised in [[Chester, Pennsylvania]], the son of Rylanda Hollis, a single mother who worked two jobs as a dietary supervisor and bartender. He grew up with older brother [[Rahlir Hollis-Jefferson|Rahlir]], who also became a professional basketball player. Their father was frequently absent and spent some time in jail.<ref name=republic>{{cite news|last=Boivin|first=Paola|title=Arizona's Hollis-Jefferson knows all about sacrifice|url=http://www.azcentral.com/story/sports/college/ua/2014/03/22/arizonas-hollis-jefferson-knows-sacrifice/6761293/|access-date=June 21, 2015|work=[[The Arizona Republic]]|date=March 25, 2014}}</ref> Hollis-Jefferson began honing his game when he was 12.<ref name=noact/> At a young age he took a strong interest in defense and acknowledged that he scored only because he was taller than his peers.<ref name=republic/>

He attended [[Chester High School (Chester, Pennsylvania)|Chester High School]] where he began an outstanding basketball career under head coach Larry Yarbray. The [[small forward]] became the first player to ever be named [[Delaware County, Pennsylvania|Delaware County]] Player of the Year for multiple seasons.<ref>{{cite web|last=Chandik|first=Matt|title=Daily Times Player of the Year: Despite setback, Chester's Rondae Jefferson should be proud|url=http://www.delcotimes.com/general-news/20130328/daily-times-player-of-the-year-despite-setback-chesters-rondae-jefferson-should-be-proud|website=DelcoTimes.com|date=March 28, 2013 |access-date=June 29, 2014}}</ref> He was also instrumental in Chester's first-ever undefeated season. The Clippers finished 91–5 in his last three years at the school and won two state titles.<ref name=cox/> In his senior year, he lost in the state title game to [[Lower Merion High School|Lower Merion]].<ref name=noact/> He finished his career with more than 1,000 points and a school-record 780 rebounds.<ref name=cox/>

Hollis-Jefferson participated in the [[2013 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|2013 McDonald's All-American Game]] against future [[Arizona Wildcats men's basketball|Arizona]] teammate, [[Aaron Gordon]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Zimmerman|first=Kevin|title=Aaron Gordon is 2013 McDonald's All-American MVP, Rondae Jefferson makes unconfirmed history|url=http://www.azdesertswarm.com/basketball/2013/4/3/4181580/aaron-gordon-2013-mcdonalds-all-american-mvp-rondae-jefferson|website=AZDesertsWarm.com|date=April 3, 2013|publisher=SBNation.com|access-date=June 29, 2014|archive-date=March 1, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140301080032/http://www.azdesertswarm.com/basketball/2013/4/3/4181580/aaron-gordon-2013-mcdonalds-all-american-mvp-rondae-jefferson|url-status=live}}</ref> Following the event, he took part in the [[Jordan Brand Classic]] with some of the most highly recruited high school stars in the nation such as [[Julius Randle]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Breen|first=Matt|title=Chester's Rondae Jefferson named to Jordan Brand Classic|url=http://www.philly.com/philly/blogs/rally/Chesters-Rondae-Jefferson-named-to-Jordan-Brand-Classic.html|website=Philly.com|access-date=June 29, 2014|archive-date=June 22, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150622050640/http://www.philly.com/philly/blogs/rally/Chesters-Rondae-Jefferson-named-to-Jordan-Brand-Classic.html|url-status=live}}</ref> At the conclusion of Hollis-Jefferson's years with the Clippers, he was tabbed the sixth-best [[small forward]] of his class by [[247Sports.com]] and the fifth best by [[Rivals.com]]. He eventually chose to attend the [[University of Arizona]] and represent the school through their successful [[basketball]] program over other possibilities such as [[Florida Gators men's basketball|Florida]] and [[Syracuse Orange men's basketball|Syracuse]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Rondae Hollis-Jefferson -Yahoo! Sports|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/ncaa/basketball/recruiting/player-Rondae-Hollis-Jefferson-125946|website=Rivals|publisher=Yahoo! Sports|access-date=June 29, 2014}}</ref>

==College career==
[[File:Rondae Hollis-Jefferson.JPG|thumb|upright|Hollis-Jefferson playing for Arizona in March 2014]]
In his freshman season with [[2013–14 Arizona Wildcats men's basketball team|Arizona]], Hollis-Jefferson became known as fierce [[Point (basketball)|scorer]], [[rebound (basketball)|rebounder]], and [[block (basketball)|shot-blocker]] despite his relatively small size. The start of his season was marked with 10 points, 5 rebounds, and 2 assists against [[2013–14 Cal Poly Mustangs men's basketball team|Cal Poly]] off the bench. He posted his first [[double-double]] in a game against [[2013–14 Oregon Ducks men's basketball team|Oregon]].<ref name=arizona/> He improved on his [[free throw]] shooting as his freshman year progressed. Throughout the season, Hollis-Jefferson mainly functioned as the team's [[sixth man]], but became a starter after [[Brandon Ashley]] was lost for the season with a foot injury in the Wildcats' 60–58 upset loss to [[2013–14 California Golden Bears men's basketball team|California]] on February 1.<ref name=noact>{{cite news|last=Santoliquito|first=Joseph|title=Rondae Hollis-Jefferson's game is no act|url=http://www.philly.com/philly/sports/colleges/20140316_Rondae_Hollis-Jefferson_s_game_is_no_act.html#wy5C0UxJYWeDHCkk.99|access-date=June 21, 2015|work=[[The Philadelphia Inquirer]]|date=March 16, 2014|archive-date=June 22, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150622043451/http://www.philly.com/philly/sports/colleges/20140316_Rondae_Hollis-Jefferson_s_game_is_no_act.html#wy5C0UxJYWeDHCkk.99|url-status=live}}</ref> Hollis-Jefferson ended up starting 6 of 38 games played due to the roster that was dominated by the likes of [[Aaron Gordon]], but still got his name on the [[Pac-12]] All-Freshman Team.<ref name=arizona>{{cite web|title=Rondae Hollis-Jefferson Bio|url=http://www.arizonawildcats.com/ViewArticle.dbml?ATCLID=208761261|website=ArizonaWildcats.com|access-date=June 29, 2014|archive-date=July 2, 2015|archive-url=https://archive.today/20150702101328/http://www.arizonawildcats.com/ViewArticle.dbml?ATCLID=208761261|url-status=live}}</ref> In his freshman year, Hollis-Jefferson averaged 9.1 points, 5.7 rebounds, and 1.4 assists per game.<ref name=cox>{{cite news|last=Cox|first=Danny|title=Rondae Hollis-Jefferson Brings Arizona In The Sweet 16 With Talent And Leadership|url=http://pittsburgh.cbslocal.com/2015/03/23/rondae-hollis-jefferson-brings-arizona-in-the-sweet-16-with-talent-and-leadership/|access-date=June 21, 2015|work=[[CBS]]|date=March 23, 2015}}</ref> "It's a lot different than just waking up, going to school and playing basketball for Chester," said Hollis-Jefferson of his freshman year. "In the beginning of the season, I was lost. But it's not about who's starting, it's about who finishes. It stuck with me for about a month or so, playing behind people. I went along with it and kept playing. I need to make people respect my shot. I know I can shoot it. I have to stay in attack mode."<ref name=noact/>

As a sophomore, Hollis-Jefferson increased his averages to 11.3 points and 6.9 rebounds per game. He improved in his leadership and offense.<ref name=cox/> As a sophomore, he was voted first-team [[List of All-Pac-12 Conference men's basketball teams|All-Pac-12]], and was named to the Pac-12 All-Defensive Team.<ref>{{cite press release|title=2014–15 Pac-12 Conference Men's Basketball Honors|date=March 9, 2015|publisher=Pac-12|url=https://pac-12.com/news/2015/3/9/2014-15-pac-12-conference-mens-basketball-honors.aspx|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150312012307/http://pac-12.com/article/2015/03/09/2014-15-pac-12-conference-mens-basketball-honors|archive-date=March 12, 2015|url-status=live}}</ref> He helped lead the Wildcats to two consecutive Elite Eight appearances in the NCAA tournament, losing to [[Wisconsin Badgers men's basketball|Wisconsin]] on both occasions. On April 7, 2015, Hollis-Jefferson declared for the [[2015 NBA draft]], forgoing his final two years of college eligibility. "I don't know if I've enjoyed coaching a player more than I've enjoyed coaching Rondae," coach [[Sean Miller]] said.<ref>{{cite web |title=Hollis-Jefferson leaving Arizona, declares for NBA Draft |url=http://www.foxsports.com/arizona/story/rondae-hollis-jefferson-leaving-arizona-declares-for-nba-draft-040715 |url-status=dead |access-date=June 20, 2015 |work=Fox Sports |archive-date=May 11, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150511042540/http://www.foxsports.com/arizona/story/rondae-hollis-jefferson-leaving-arizona-declares-for-nba-draft-040715 }}</ref>

==Professional career==

===Brooklyn Nets (2015–2019)===
On June 25, 2015, Hollis-Jefferson was selected by the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] with the 23rd overall pick in the [[2015 NBA draft]]. rookie-scale contract with the Nets.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/nets/nets-sign-rondae-hollis-jefferson|title=NETS SIGN RONDAE Log|work=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=December 8, 2015|archive-date=December 4, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151204191605/http://www.basketball-reference.com/players/h/holliro01/gamelog/2016|url-status=live}}</ref> On December 7, he was diagnosed with a returned to action in late March.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160322/CHABKN/gameinfo.html|title=Batum scores 23 points, Hornets beat Nets 105–100|work=NBA.com|date=March 22, On November 12, 2016, Hollis-Jefferson scored a then career-high 20 points and tied a career high with 13 rebounds in a 122–104 win over the [[Phoenix Suns]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899589|title=Nets finish strong, beat Suns 122–104 for first road win|work=ESPN.com|date=November 12, 2016|access-date=November 13, 2016}}</ref>

On December 14, 2017, Hollis-Jefferson scored a career-high 25 points on 10-for-16 shooting in a 111–104 loss to the [[New York Knicks]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975165|title=Knicks hold on to beat Nets after Porzingis leaves|work=ESPN.com|date=December 14, 2017|access-date=December 14, 2017}}</ref> He strained his right groin during a 116–91 loss to the [[Milwaukee Bucks]] on January 26, returning to action on February 26 against the Chicago Bulls after missing the Nets' previous 11 games.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975645|title=Crabbe scores 21, Nets top Bulls 104–87 to snap 8-game skid|work=ESPN.com|date=February 26, 2018|access-date=February 26, 2018|archive-date=February 27, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180227213934/http://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975645|url-status=live}}</ref>

Hollis-Jefferson missed the first three games of the 2018–19 season with a hip injury and the birth of his first child.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401070734|title=Russell, Harris lead Nets past winless Cavaliers 102–86|work=ESPN.com|date=October 24, 2018|access-date=October 24, 2018|archive-date=October 25, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181025150011/http://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401070734|url-status=live}}</ref> On November 28, 2018, in a 101–91 loss to the [[Utah Jazz]], Hollis-Jefferson had 14 points and a season-high 11 rebounds for his first double-double.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401070989|title=Mitchell returns, carries Jazz to 101–91 victory over Nets|work=ESPN.com|date=November 28, 2018|access-date=November 28, 2018|archive-date=November 29, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181129061031/http://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401070989|url-status=live}}</ref> On March 19, 2019, he made a layup with eight-tenths of a second remaining to lift the Nets to a 123–121 win over the [[Sacramento Kings]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071736|title=Nets, down 25 in 4th, storm back to shock Kings|work=ESPN.com|date=March 19, 2019|access-date=March 20, 2019|archive-date=May 11, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190511024506/http://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071736|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last=Dowd|first=Tom|url=https://www.nba.com/nets/news/sidebar/2019/03/19/rondae-hollis-jefferson-delivers-game-winner-to-lift-brooklyn-nets|title=RONDAE HOLLIS-JEFFERSON DELIVERS GAME-WINNER TO LIFT BROOKLYN NETS|work=NBA.com|date=March 20, 2019|access-date=March 20, 2019|archive-date=March 21, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190321010513/https://www.nba.com/nets/news/sidebar/2019/03/19/rondae-hollis-jefferson-delivers-game-winner-to-lift-brooklyn-nets|url-status=live}}</ref>

On June 17, the Nets opted not to make Hollis-Jefferson a qualifying offer, making him an unrestricted free agent.

===Toronto Raptors (2019–2020)===
On July 18, 2019, Hollis-Jefferson signed with the defending champion, [[Toronto Raptors]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/raptors/press-release/raptors-sign-rondae-hollis-jefferson|title=Raptors Sign Rondae Hollis-Jefferson|last=Naje|first=B.|work=NBA.com|date=July 18, 2019|access-date=July 18, 2019}}</ref>

On December 3, 2020, Hollis-Jefferson signed a non-guaranteed preseason contract with the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/timberwolves/news/timberwolves-sign-rondae-hollis-jefferson|title=Timberwolves sign Rondae Hollis-Jefferson|work=NBA.com|date=December 3, 2020|access-date=December 3, 2020}}</ref> He was waived by the Timberwolves shortly after he signed on December 19, 2020.<ref>{{cite web |date=December 19, 2020 |title=Timberwolves Waive Four Players |url=https://www.nba.com/timberwolves/news/timberwolves-waive-four-players |access-date=April 8, 2021 |work=NBA.com |archive-date=January 10, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210110015318/https://www.nba.com/timberwolves/news/timberwolves-waive-four-players |url-status=live }}</ref>

===Portland Trail Blazers (2021)===
On April 8, 2021, Hollis-Jefferson signed a 10-day contract with the [[Portland Trail Blazers]].<ref>{{cite web |date=April 8, 2021 |title=Trail Blazers Sign Rondae Hollis-Jefferson to 10-Day Contract |url=https://www.nba.com/blazers/news/2021/4/8/blazers-sign-rondae-hollis-jefferson-to-10-day |access-date=April 8, 2021 |work=NBA.com}}</ref> On April 18, he signed a second 10-day contract<ref>{{cite web |date=April 18, 2021 |title=Trail Blazers Sign Rondae Hollis-Jefferson to Second 10-Day Contract |url=https://www.nba.com/blazers/news/2021/4/18/blazers-sign-rondae-hollis-jefferson-to-second-10-day |access-date=April 18, 2021 |work=NBA.com |archive-date=April 18, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210418150147/https://www.nba.com/blazers/news/2021/4/18/blazers-sign-rondae-hollis-jefferson-to-second-10-day |url-status=live }}</ref> and 10 days later, he signed for the rest of the season after appearing in six games.<ref>{{cite web |last=Holdahl |first=Casey |date=April 28, 2021 |title=Trail Blazers Sign Rondae Hollis-Jefferson for Remainder of 2020-21 Season |url=https://www.nba.com/blazers/trail-blazers-sign-rondae-hollis-jefferson-remainder-2020-21-season |access-date=April 28, 2021 |work=NBA.com |archive-date=April 28, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210428190851/https://www.nba.com/blazers/trail-blazers-sign-rondae-hollis-jefferson-remainder-2020-21-season |url-status=live }}</ref>

===Beşiktaş (2021–2022)===
On September 28, 2021, Hollis-Jefferson signed with [[Beşiktaş J.K. (men's basketball)|Beşiktaş Icrypex]] of the [[Basketball Super League|Basketbol Süper Ligi]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Beşiktaş Icrypex strengthen roster with American power forward|url=https://bjk.com.tr/en/news/81773/besiktas-icrypex-strengthen-roster-with-american-power-forward.html|website=BJK.com.tr|date=September 28, 2021|access-date=October 3, 2021|archive-date=October 4, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211004032437/https://bjk.com.tr/en/news/81773/besiktas-icrypex-strengthen-roster-with-american-power-forward.html|url-status=live}}</ref> He scored a career-high 26 points in a 69–82 loss over the Rytas.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.eurobasket.com/boxScores/Basketball%20Champions%20League/2021/1117_683_1035.asp|title=Besiktas 69 – Rytas 82|publisher=EuroBasket|date=November 17, 2021|accessdate=May 12, 2022|archive-date=February 17, 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250217112348/https://www.eurobasket.com/boxScores/Basketball%20Champions%20League/2021/1117_683_1035.asp|url-status=live}}</ref>

===Atléticos de San Germán (2022)===
On April 11, 2022, Hollis-Jefferson signed with [[Atléticos de San Germán]] of the [[Baloncesto Superior Nacional]].<ref>{{cite news|first=Dario|last=Skerletic|title=Rondae Hollis-Jefferson signs with Atleticos de San German|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/rondae-hollis-jefferson-signs-with-atleticos-de-san-german/|newspaper=Sportando|date=April 11, 2022|access-date=April 11, 2022|archive-date=April 11, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220411174308/https://sportando.basketball/en/rondae-hollis-jefferson-signs-with-atleticos-de-san-german/|url-status=live}}</ref> He played 31 games and averaged 19.7 points per game. On May 16, 2023, Hollis-Jefferson was brought back by Atléticos de San Germán.<ref>{{cite web |title=Latin American basketball News, Scores, Stats, Analysis, Standings |url=https://basketball.latinbasket.com/Puerto-Rico/news/809954/Hollis-Jefferson-is-back-at-San-German-ex-TNT-Tropang |website=basketball.latinbasket.com |access-date=September 23, 2023}}</ref> He played 22 games and averaged 21.7 points per game.

===TNT Tropang Giga (2023–2024)===
In February 2023, Hollis-Jefferson signed with the [[TNT Tropang Giga]] of the [[Philippine Basketball Association]] (PBA) to replace [[Jalen Hudson]] as the team's import for the [[2023 PBA Governors' Cup]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Ramos|first=Gerry|url=https://www.spin.ph/basketball/pba/tnt-replaces-import-jalen-hudson-with-rondae-hollis-jefferson-a793-20230213|title=Co-leader TNT replacing Jalen Hudson with Rondae Hollis-Jefferson|website=Spin.ph|date=February 13, 2023|accessdate=February 13, 2023}}</ref> He played 16 games and averaged 30.4 points per game. On May 30, 2023, it was announced that Hollis-Jefferson will return as the team's import for the [[2023–24 PBA Commissioner's Cup]].<ref>{{cite web |title=TNT bringing back Hollis-Jefferson for PBA Comm's Cup |url=https://fastbreak.com.ph/tnt-bringing-back-hollis-jefferson-for-pba-comms-cup/ |website=fastbreak.com.ph |access-date=September 23, 2023 |date=May 30, 2023}}</ref>

===TNT Tropang Giga (2024–present)===
In August 2024, Hollis-Jefferson returns to TNT as the team's import for the [[2024 PBA Governors' Cup]].<ref>{{cite web |first=Reuben |last=Terrado |url=https://www.spin.ph/basketball/pba/rhj-return-to-tnt-official-for-pba-season-49-governors-cup-a795-20240814 |title=RHJ return to TNT official for PBA Season 49 Governors' Cup |website=Spin.ph |date=August 14, 2024 |accessdate=August 14, 2024 |archive-date=August 14, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240814064807/https://www.spin.ph/basketball/pba/rhj-return-to-tnt-official-for-pba-season-49-governors-cup-a795-20240814 |url-status=live }}</ref> He helped the team clinch their second consecutive Governors' Cup title, scoring 31 points in a series-clinching 95–85 victory against the [[Barangay Ginebra San Miguel]] in Game 6 of the [[2024 PBA Governors' Cup finals|Governors' Cup finals]].<ref>{{Cite web|last=Dioquino|first=Delfin|url=https://www.rappler.com/sports/pba/governors-cup-finals-results-barangay-ginebra-tnt-tropang-giga-november-8-2024/|title=Back-to-back: TNT repeats over Barangay Ginebra to defend Governors' Cup title in Game 6|publisher=[[Rappler]]|date=November 8, 2024|access-date=November 22, 2024}}</ref> After the championship in Governos' Cup, Hollis-Jefferson helped TNT captured the Commissioner's Cup against Barangay Ginebra in Finals Game 7, giving TNT a back-to-back championships in one season. Hollis-Jefferson received His 3rd Best Import of the Conference award.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://sports.inquirer.net/616031/tnt-conquers-ginebra-in-game-7-classic-to-win-11th-pba-title|title=TNT conquers Ginebra in Game 7 classic to win 11th PBA title|publisher=inquirer.net|date=March 28, 2025|access-date=February 12, 2026|archive-date=April 29, 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250429153801/https://sports.inquirer.net/616031/tnt-conquers-ginebra-in-game-7-classic-to-win-11th-pba-title|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.onesports.ph/pba/article/30218/tnt-s-rondae-hollis-jefferson-named-pba-best-import-a-3rd-time|title=TNT's Rondae Hollis-Jefferson named PBA Best Import a 3rd time|publisher=One Sports PH|date=March 21, 2025|access-date=February 12, 2026|archive-date=May 23, 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250523233808/https://www.onesports.ph/pba/article/30218/tnt-s-rondae-hollis-jefferson-named-pba-best-import-a-3rd-time|url-status=live}}</ref>
In April 2025, Hollis-Jefferson signed 1-year "exclusive" contract for the TNT.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Dioquino|first=Delfin|url=https://www.spin.ph/basketball/pba/tnt-signs-rondae-hollis-jefferson-to-one-year-contract-a793-20250420|title=TNT signs Rondae Hollis-Jefferson to 'exclusive' one-year contract|publisher=Spin.ph|date=April 20, 2025|access-date=February 12, 2026|archive-date=August 6, 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250806085456/https://www.spin.ph/basketball/pba/tnt-signs-rondae-hollis-jefferson-to-one-year-contract-a793-20250420|url-status=live}}</ref> In September 2025, TNT allowed Hollis-Jefferson to play for its sister-team [[Meralco Bolts]] for their campaign on [[East Asia Super League]].<ref>{{Cite web|last=Dioquino|first=Delfin|url=https://www.spin.ph/basketball/pba/meralco-bolts-sign-israel-romero-as-second-import-for-easl-a793-20250910|title=PBA Meralco taps Puerto Rico national player to join RHJ, Brownlee|publisher=Spin.ph|date=September 10, 2025|access-date= February 12, 2026}}</ref>

===Meralco Bolts (2025)===
On September 11, 2025, Hollis-Jefferson joined the [[Meralco Bolts]] of the [[East Asia Super League]] as an import.<ref>{{cite web |first=Jan |last=Ballesteros |url=https://www.onesports.ph/pba/article/35478/rhj-brownlee-ismael-romero-reinforce-meralco-in-upcoming-easl-season |title=Rondae Hollis-Jefferson, Justin Brownlee, Ismael Romero reinforce Meralco in EASL season |website=One Sports |date=September 11, 2025 |accessdate=September 11, 2025 }}</ref> In a December 6 game against the [[Macau Black Bears]], Hollis-Jefferson suffered a [[Achilles tendon rupture|ruptured Achilles tendon]], ending his season.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Rondae Hollis-Jefferson suffers ruptured Achilles tendon|url=https://sports.inquirer.net/652319/rondae-hollis-jefferson-suffers-ruptured-achilles-tendon/amp|access-date=December 17, 2025|website=sports.inquirer.net|language=en}}</ref>

==Philanthropy and community work==
In June 2025, Hollis-Jefferson launched '''''RHJ on Tour''''', a nationwide grassroots basketball initiative in the [[Philippines]] in partnership with [[TNT Tropang 5G|TNT Tropang Giga/5G]] and [[Smart Communications]].<ref name="PhilstarLaunch">{{cite news |last1=Henson |first1=Joaquin |title=RHJ on Tour: Tropa's gift to young kids |url=https://www.philstar.com/sports/2025/06/19/2451647/rhj-tour-tropas-gift-young-kids |work=The Philippine Star |date=June 19, 2025 |access-date=February 12, 2026}}</ref> The tour was developed as a "give-back" program to mark the 25th anniversary of the TNT franchise and aimed to provide free, professional-level training to young athletes in underserved areas.<ref name="TribuneInspires">{{cite news |title='RHJ on Tour' inspires young cagers |url=https://tribune.net.ph/2025/06/10/rhj-on-tour-inspires-young-cagers |work=Daily Tribune |date=June 10, 2025 |access-date=February 12, 2026}}</ref>

The clinics ran every weekend through July 2025, reaching over 500 youth participants across nine major stops. Hollis-Jefferson was joined by a coaching staff of [[Philippine Basketball Association|PBA]] veterans, including [[Jayson Castro]], [[Ranidel de Ocampo]], [[Bong Ravena]], and team manager [[Jojo Lastimosa]].<ref name="AllStarMag">{{cite web |last1=Ganglani |first1=Naveen |title=Hollis-Jefferson Leads Free Nationwide Clinics for Filipino Youth |url=https://all-starmagazine.com/community/hollis-jefferson-leads-free-nationwide-clinics-for-filipino-youth/ |website=All-Star Magazine |date=June 16, 2025 |access-date=February 12, 2026 |archive-date=January 18, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260118103107/https://all-starmagazine.com/community/hollis-jefferson-leads-free-nationwide-clinics-for-filipino-youth/ |url-status=live }}</ref> 

Locations for the tour included: 

'''Luzon:''' [[Quezon City]], [[Batangas]], [[Vigan]], and [[Baguio]].
'''Visayas:''' [[Cebu City]], [[Bacolod]], and [[Iloilo City]].

The curriculum emphasized a "holistic" approach to sports, blending technical skills like footwork and shooting with motivational talks on the importance of education, family respect, and discipline.<ref name="SunStarCamp">{{cite news |title=TNT Tropang 5G rolls out 'RHJ on Tour' basketball camp for free |url=https://www.sunstar.com.ph/davao/tnt-tropang-5g-rolls-out-rhj-on-tour-basketball-camp-for-free |work=SunStar Davao |date=June 10, 2025 |access-date=February 12, 2026 |archive-date=January 18, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260118232258/https://www.sunstar.com.ph/davao/tnt-tropang-5g-rolls-out-rhj-on-tour-basketball-camp-for-free |url-status=live }}</ref>

The initiative was chronicled in a documentary-style series titled ''RHJ on Tour'', produced by [[Smart Communications|Smart Sports]] and released on [[YouTube]]. The series focused on the regional basketball cultures of the Philippines, such as the historic basketball roots in Cebu and the community-driven "teamwork beyond the game" in Vigan.<ref name="SmartYouTube">{{cite web |title=RHJ on Tour Episode 5: Cebu Legacy |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OqM4YX4lha8 |website=YouTube |publisher=Smart Sports |date=November 12, 2025 |access-date=February 12, 2026}}</ref> 

Hollis-Jefferson further demonstrated his commitment to the local community in late 2025 by pledging his PBA Best Import cash prize to the Alagang Kapatid Foundation to support typhoon relief efforts.<ref name="OneSportsRelief">{{cite web |title=PBA: Rondae Hollis-Jefferson to donate Best Import reward to Alagang Kapatid Foundation |url=https://www.onesports.ph/pba/article/26138/pba-rondae-hollis-jefferson-to-donate-best-import-reward-to-alagang-kapatid-foundation |website=One Sports |date=November 8, 2025 |access-date=February 12, 2026 |archive-date=January 14, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260114134118/https://www.onesports.ph/pba/article/26138/pba-rondae-hollis-jefferson-to-donate-best-import-reward-to-alagang-kapatid-foundation |url-status=live }}</ref>

JBF |language=en |via=Facebook}}</ref> On August 16, 2023, he was included in [[Jordan]]'s 17-man squad for the [[2023 FIBA Basketball World Cup]].<ref>{{Cite tweet |number=1691777065974976994 |user=FIBAWC |title=Falcons committed for Jordan’s third appearance at #FIBAWC 🏆 |access-date=August 16, 2023 |language=en |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230816222152/https://twitter.com/FIBAWC/status/1691777065974976994?s=20 |archive-date=August 16, 2023 |url-status=live |website=Twitter}}</ref> On August 28, 2023, Hollis-Jefferson drew comparisons to the late [[Kobe Bryant]] for his play with the Jordan national team during the 2023 FIBA Basketball World Cup.<ref>{{cite news |last=Kalbrosky |first=Bryan |date=August 28, 2023 |title=Ex-NBA player Rondae Hollis-Jefferson re-emerged as a Kobe Bryant clone at the FIBA World Cup |url=https://ftw.usatoday.com/2023/08/rondae-hollis-jefferson-kobe-clone-jordan-fiba-world-cup |access-date=September 5, 2023 |website=[[USA Today]]}}</ref>

The [[Samahang Basketball ng Pilipinas]] of the Philippines also offered Hollis-Jefferson to play for their national team but he eventually chose Jordan.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Ramos |first1=Gerry |date=September 22, 2023 |title=Why RHJ chose Jordan over SBP offer to become Gilas naturalized player |url=https://www.spin.ph/basketball/fiba/rondae-hollis-jefferson-naturalization-prospect-sbp-gilas-pilipinas-jordan-a793-20230922 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231104084440/https://www.spin.ph/basketball/fiba/rondae-hollis-jefferson-naturalization-prospect-sbp-gilas-pilipinas-jordan-a793-20230922 |archive-date=November 4, 2023 |access-date=September 24, 2023 |work=Sports Interactive Network Philippines |language=en}}</ref>

==Player profile==
Hollis-Jefferson plays both [[Forward (basketball)|forward]] positions. Using his athleticism and {{convert|7|ft|2|in|adj=on}} [[wingspan]], he is part of the NBA trend of undersized [[power forward (basketball)|power forwards]].<ref>{{cite news|last=Fonseca|first=Bryan|title=Rondae becoming a fixture at power forward|work=SBNation|url=https://www.netsdaily.com/2017/2/12/14592372/rondae-becoming-a-fixture-at-power-forward|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170817094908/https://www.netsdaily.com/platform/amp/2017/2/12/14592372/rondae-becoming-a-fixture-at-power-forward|archive-date=August 17, 2017|url-status=live}}</ref>
